title: Singular band Induced by Long-Range Interaction Enables Unsplit Spreading of Localized Excitations
summary: In conventional lattice models, the dispersion relation $ω(k)$ is assumed to be a smooth function which is periodic over the first Brillouin Zone. However, in subwavelength atom arrays the dispersion of the light-mediated long-range interaction is singular at the light cone. This observation prompts us to ask what effect arises from such band singularity. Here we demonstrate that, due to the topology of smooth functions defined over the periodic Brillouin zone, smoothness implies the splitting of an initially localized excitation into counter-propagating wave packets.
